rationale: Chapter-organizing term naming each of three cosmic descent-ascent movements ('first/second/third ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ'). Each ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ is described as 'the one that comes (ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲏⲩ) upon X' and effects a roundtrip from the upper region down to bodies/corpses/trees and back. Best semantic alignment is with ⲧⲁⲍⲙ 'summon, call' (already in glossary). 'Summons' preserves the active-vocative quality: a divine call that goes out and draws light back. Confidence moderate; alternatives 'calling,' 'descent,' 'circulation' all defensible.

Lycopolitan ⲉⲣⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'temples' (plural of ⲣ̄ⲡⲉ). Distinguished from ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ 'heavens' on the same page: ⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲏⲩⲉ are architectural structures within the heavens, paired with 'dwellings' (ⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲡⲉ) and 'cities' (ⲡⲧⲟⲗⲓⲥ) at lines 13-14, 16.

Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲟⲡⲧⲉ 'preparation, equipment, ordered arrangement.' Used twice on this page in cosmological inventories: 'the array of those of heaven' (line 17) and 'the other array of cattle' (line 28). Captures both the preparatory/fitted sense and the classificatory sense of an ordered set.
Recurring verb (lines 26, 27) of the descending motion of vices upon men and cattle. Likely Lyc. extension of ϣⲱⲣ 'spread' / ϣⲱⲣϣ̄ 'pour, scatter.' Tentative.

Form unattested in our glossary. Context: 'the Life comes up out of the ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲍ of these lands.' Best candidates: (a) ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲍ 'form, structure' (Lyc. for ⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄); (b) variant of ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fullness'; (c) cosmological 'depth.' 'Depth' best matches the ascent-from-below pattern central to this kephalaion.
Coptic ϣⲛϣ 'stroke, blow, scourge' (Crum 569b). Listed with Error and venom (line 29) as ills poured down upon creatures of flesh. Confidence moderate.
Lyc. ⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ = Sah. ⲃⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'anger, wrath.' Listed with desire (ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ) and evil (ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ) as the moral-affective triad in lines 25 and 31.
Lycopolitan iterative-habitual prefix marking 3pl subjects in habitual/repeated actions: ϣⲁⲗⲩϣⲟⲣⲱϩ 'they pour down (habitually),' ϣⲁⲗⲩⲣ̄ⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'they shall abound.' Distinct from simple future ⲥⲉⲛⲁ-.
